description: The intelligence library's guideline set, scoped by what the deliverable actually contains. Guidelines already carried by a Pointer, Polish, or Slop gate are not repeated here.

gates.title: Alt Text On Meaningful Images
gates.rule: Every image that carries meaning has descriptive alt text; decorative images have empty alt.

gates.title: Icon-Only Buttons Have Accessible Names
gates.rule: aria-label on icon-only buttons, accessibilityLabel in native. An unlabelled icon button is invisible to a screen reader.

gates.title: Tab Order Matches Visual Order
gates.rule: Full keyboard operation, and the tab sequence follows the reading order. No positive tabindex.

gates.title: Form Labels Are Real Labels
gates.rule: Every field has a visible label element bound with for. Placeholder-only labelling fails as soon as the field has content.

gates.title: Skip Link To Main Content
gates.rule: A keyboard user can jump past the navigation to the main content.

gates.title: Heading Hierarchy Is Sequential
gates.rule: h1 through h6 in order, no skipped level, one h1 per page.

gates.title: Colour Is Never The Only Signal
gates.rule: Error, success, selected, and required states carry an icon, shape, or word alongside the colour.

gates.title: Text Scaling Does Not Break Layout
gates.rule: The layout survives system text scaling and Dynamic Type at its largest setting without truncation or overlap.

gates.title: Screen Reader Order And Roles Are Right
gates.rule: Reading order is logical, roles and states (selected, disabled, expanded) are announced, and hints are meaningful.

gates.title: Modals And Multi-Step Flows Have An Escape
gates.rule: A visible cancel or back route out of every modal and every step of a flow, plus Escape on desktop.

gates.title: System And Accessibility Shortcuts Preserved
gates.rule: Nothing overrides system or assistive shortcuts, and drag-and-drop has a keyboard alternative.

gates.title: Focus Moves To Main On Route Change
gates.rule: After a page transition, focus lands on the main content region so screen reader users are not stranded at the top.

gates.title: 8px Between Touch Targets
gates.rule: Neighbouring targets keep at least 8px of separation so a near-miss does not fire the wrong control.

gates.title: Primary Actions Do Not Depend On Hover
gates.rule: Anything essential is reachable by click or tap. Hover-only affordances do not exist on touch.

gates.title: Errors Appear Next To Their Cause
gates.rule: The error message sits by the thing that caused it, in plain words, with the way out.

gates.title: No Horizontal Swipe On Main Content
gates.rule: Main content scrolls vertically. Horizontal swipe is reserved for carousels and back gestures, and never fights them.

gates.title: Platform Gestures Behave As Expected
gates.rule: Swipe-back, pinch-zoom, and pull-to-refresh keep their standard meanings, and system gestures are not blocked.

gates.title: Gestures Have A Visible Alternative
gates.rule: Nothing critical is gesture-only. Swipe actions show an affordance - a chevron, a label, a peek.

gates.title: Safe Areas Are Respected
gates.rule: Primary targets stay clear of the notch, Dynamic Island, gesture bar, and screen edges.

gates.title: No Pixel-Perfect Precision Required
gates.rule: No tap depends on hitting a small icon or a thin edge exactly.

gates.title: Haptics Are Used Sparingly
gates.rule: Haptic feedback confirms important actions and nothing else.

gates.title: Images Are Optimised And Responsive
gates.rule: WebP or AVIF, srcset and sizes for the widths in play, lazy loading below the fold, eager and fetchpriority high on the LCP image.

gates.title: Images Declare Their Box
gates.rule: width and height attributes or an aspect-ratio, so nothing shifts as they load.

gates.title: Fonts Load Without Blanking Text
gates.rule: font-display: swap or optional, space reserved to limit shift, and only genuinely critical faces preloaded.

gates.title: Above-The-Fold CSS Is Prioritised
gates.rule: Critical CSS is inline or loaded first; the rest does not block the first paint.

gates.title: Non-Critical Code Is Split Out
gates.rule: Route-level or feature-level splitting, dynamic import for anything below the fold or behind an interaction.

gates.title: Third-Party Scripts Are Async And Audited
gates.rule: Every third-party tag is async or defer, and every one still on the page has a reason to be.

gates.title: Async Content Reserves Its Space
gates.rule: Space is held for content that arrives late, so nothing below it jumps.

gates.title: Long Lists Are Virtualised
gates.rule: Past roughly 50 items, the list virtualises rather than rendering everything.

gates.title: Frame Budget Is Respected
gates.rule: Per-frame work stays under 16ms; heavy work moves off the main thread. High-frequency events are debounced or throttled.

gates.title: Offline And Slow Networks Degrade Gracefully
gates.rule: An offline state says so, and slow connections get lower-resolution images and less motion rather than a hang.

gates.title: Style Matches The Product Type
gates.rule: The visual language is chosen for what this product is, from the intelligence library, not picked by habit.

gates.title: One Style Across Every Screen
gates.rule: The same style language, effects, radii, and shadow scale hold across every page and component in the deliverable.

gates.title: Palette Comes From The Product Or Brand
gates.rule: The palette is drawn from the brand, or from the product and industry via the palette library - never invented mid-build.

gates.title: Effects Match The Chosen Style
gates.rule: Shadow, blur, and radius agree with the style. Glass effects on a flat design are two designs fighting.

gates.title: Elevation Follows One Scale
gates.rule: Cards, sheets, and modals sit on a consistent elevation scale. Random shadow values are the tell.

gates.title: Platform Idioms Are Respected
gates.rule: iOS follows HIG, Android follows Material - navigation, controls, typography, and motion each follow their platform.

gates.title: Native Controls Preferred Over Custom
gates.rule: System controls unless branding genuinely requires a custom one; a custom control inherits none of the accessibility work.

gates.title: Blur Means Dismissal, Not Decoration
gates.rule: Background blur signals that the layer behind is dismissable. It is not a texture.

gates.title: One Primary Action Per Screen
gates.rule: A single primary CTA; everything else is visually subordinate. Two primaries is none.

gates.title: Light And Dark Are Designed Together
gates.rule: The dark variant is designed, not derived by inversion - desaturated tonal variants, contrast verified separately.

gates.title: Viewport Meta Is Correct And Zoom Is Not Disabled
gates.rule: width=device-width, initial-scale=1, and no maximum-scale or user-scalable=no.

gates.title: Mobile First, Then Scaled Up
gates.rule: Base styles are the small screen; breakpoints add rather than undo.

gates.title: Breakpoints Are Systematic
gates.rule: One breakpoint set across the deliverable - 375, 768, 1024, 1440 or the project's own - not a new width per component.

gates.title: Body Text Is At Least 16px On Mobile
gates.rule: Under 16px, iOS zooms the page on focus and the text is hard to read anyway.

gates.title: Line Length Is Controlled
gates.rule: 35-60 characters on mobile, 60-75 on desktop.

gates.title: Consistent Container Width
gates.rule: One max-width for content on desktop, applied consistently rather than per section.

gates.title: Z-Index Comes From A Scale
gates.rule: A named layer scale - base, dropdown, sticky, overlay, modal, toast. No 9999.

gates.title: Fixed Bars Reserve Space For Content
gates.rule: A fixed nav or bottom bar has matching padding on the scroll container, so nothing hides underneath it.

gates.title: No Nested Scroll Traps
gates.rule: Inner scroll regions do not fight the page scroll.

gates.title: Dynamic Viewport Units On Mobile
gates.rule: min-h-dvh rather than 100vh, so the mobile browser chrome does not cut the layout.

gates.title: Landscape Is Usable
gates.rule: The layout stays readable and operable in landscape, including on a short viewport.

gates.title: Core Content Comes First On Mobile
gates.rule: The important content is above the fold on a phone; secondary content folds or moves down.

gates.title: Hierarchy Is Not Carried By Colour Alone
gates.rule: Size, weight, and spacing establish the hierarchy; colour reinforces it.

gates.title: Gutters Adapt By Width
gates.rule: Horizontal insets grow with the viewport rather than holding a phone gutter on a desktop.

gates.title: Body Line-Height Is 1.5-1.75
gates.rule: Tighter than 1.5 on body copy is a wall of text.

gates.title: Type Scale Is Consistent
gates.rule: One scale - 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 32 or the project's own - used everywhere. Sizes off the scale are arbitrary.

gates.title: Heading And Body Faces Pair
gates.rule: The two faces have compatible personalities, from the pairing library rather than picked apart.

gates.title: Weight Reinforces Hierarchy
gates.rule: 600-700 headings, 400 body, 500 labels. Weight is doing work, not decoration.

gates.title: Semantic Colour Tokens In Components
gates.rule: Components reference primary, surface, on-surface, error - never a raw value.

gates.title: Wrapping Preferred Over Truncation
gates.rule: Text wraps where it can. Where it must truncate, an ellipsis plus the full text on hover or expand.

gates.title: Tabular Figures For Data
gates.rule: Prices, timers, and data columns use tabular numerals so digits do not jitter as they change.

gates.title: Letter-Spacing Left Alone On Body
gates.rule: Platform defaults on body copy; tracking adjustments belong to display type only.

gates.title: Whitespace Groups And Separates
gates.rule: Space is used to group related items and separate unrelated ones, not distributed evenly to fill.

gates.title: Helper Text Is Persistent
gates.rule: Complex fields carry helper text below them, not inside the placeholder where it vanishes on focus.

gates.title: Validation Fires On Blur
gates.rule: Errors appear once the user has finished the field, not on every keystroke.

gates.title: Semantic Input Types
gates.rule: email, tel, number, url - so the mobile keyboard matches the field.

gates.title: Autocomplete Attributes Present
gates.rule: autocomplete or textContentType on name, email, address, and payment fields so the system can fill them.

gates.title: Password Fields Have A Show Toggle
gates.rule: A visible show/hide control on every password field.

gates.title: Required Fields Are Marked
gates.rule: Required is indicated visually and in the accessibility tree.

gates.title: Submit Has Loading Then Result
gates.rule: The submit control moves through pending to success or error; it never sits idle after a click.

gates.title: Errors Announce Themselves
gates.rule: role="alert" or an aria-live region on validation errors, so a screen reader hears them.

gates.title: Focus Moves To The First Invalid Field
gates.rule: After a failed submit, focus lands on the first field that needs fixing.

gates.title: Multiple Errors Get A Summary
gates.rule: More than one error shows a summary at the top with anchor links to each field.

gates.title: Error Text Says Cause And Fix
gates.rule: Not 'Invalid input'. What is wrong, and what to do about it.

gates.title: Destructive Actions Confirm
gates.rule: A confirmation before anything destructive, in the danger colour, spatially separated from the primary action.

gates.title: Destructive And Bulk Actions Offer Undo
gates.rule: An undo path, not just a confirmation dialog, wherever the action can be reversed.

gates.title: Empty States Say What To Do
gates.rule: An empty list explains why it is empty and offers the action that fills it.

gates.title: Toasts Auto-Dismiss And Do Not Steal Focus
gates.rule: 3-5 seconds, aria-live polite, focus stays where the user left it.

gates.title: Long Forms Autosave
gates.rule: A long form keeps a draft so an accidental dismissal does not cost the work, and a sheet with unsaved changes confirms before closing.

gates.title: Complexity Is Revealed Progressively
gates.rule: Advanced options unfold rather than greeting the user all at once.

gates.title: Related Fields Are Grouped
gates.rule: fieldset and legend, or a clear visual grouping, for fields that belong together.

gates.title: Read-Only Differs From Disabled
gates.rule: Read-only reads as information; disabled reads as unavailable. They do not look the same.

gates.title: Mobile Inputs Are At Least 44px Tall
gates.rule: Input height meets the touch target floor, and matches the height of adjacent buttons.

gates.title: Multi-Step Flows Show Progress And Go Back
gates.rule: A step indicator, and backward navigation that keeps what was entered.

gates.title: Timeouts Say So And Offer Retry
gates.rule: A request that times out reports it and offers the retry, rather than spinning.

gates.title: Autofill Does Not Repaint The Field
gates.rule: A browser-autofilled input paints its own background — the yellow in Chrome and Safari, a blue in some builds — straight over the field's surface token, and it survives a plain background-color rule. Untreated, every returning visitor sees a form that does not match the page, and in dark mode the autofilled text goes near-invisible on it. Override it in all three themes.

check.message: No :-webkit-autofill override on a deliverable with input fields.

gates.fix: Cover the paint with an inset shadow and set the text colour explicitly: input:-webkit-autofill { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 100px var(--surface); -webkit-text-fill-color: var(--ink); caret-color: var(--ink); transition: background-color 0s 600000s; } and repeat it for :hover, :focus, and :active.

gates.title: Current Location Is Visible In The Nav
gates.rule: The active destination is marked by colour, weight, or an indicator - never left to the user to work out.

gates.title: Navigation Stays In The Same Place
gates.rule: Placement does not change between page types.

gates.title: Nav Items Carry Icon And Label
gates.rule: Icon-only navigation costs discoverability. Bottom navigation caps at five items.

gates.title: Primary And Secondary Nav Are Separated
gates.rule: Tabs or bottom bar for top-level; drawer or settings for secondary. Not mixed at the same level.

gates.title: Back Is Predictable And Restores State
gates.rule: Back returns to where the user was, with scroll position, filters, and input intact. The stack is never silently reset.

gates.title: Every Key Screen Has A URL
gates.rule: Deep-linkable and shareable; no state that exists only after a click path.

gates.title: Modals Are Not Navigation
gates.rule: A modal is a detour, not a step in the primary path.

gates.title: Modals Have A Clear Dismiss
gates.rule: A visible close, Escape on desktop, swipe-down on mobile.

gates.title: Search Is Reachable And Helpful
gates.rule: Search sits in the top bar or a tab, and offers recent or suggested queries.

gates.title: Breadcrumbs Past Three Levels
gates.rule: Hierarchies three or more levels deep show where the user is.

gates.title: Overflow Menu Rather Than Cramming
gates.rule: Actions beyond the available space go into an overflow menu.

gates.title: Large Screens Get A Sidebar
gates.rule: At 1024px and up, a sidebar; below, bottom or top navigation.

gates.title: Destructive Items Sit Apart In Menus
gates.rule: Delete account and logout are separated from ordinary navigation, visually and spatially.

gates.title: Unavailable Destinations Explain Themselves
gates.rule: A destination the user cannot reach says why rather than vanishing.

gates.title: Core Navigation Stays Reachable
gates.rule: Navigation is not hidden entirely inside sub-flows.

gates.title: A New Page Opens At The Top
gates.rule: Navigating to a new page puts the reader at the top of it. Client-side routing keeps the scroll position by default, so arriving at a page already scrolled halfway down is the norm unless something resets it - and the reader has no idea they are looking at the middle of something. Going back is the exception: that restores the position it was left at.
gates.fix: Scroll to the top on pathname change - ScrollRestoration in React Router, or a useEffect on the pathname calling window.scrollTo({ top: 0 }) - while leaving back and forward to restore their own positions.

gates.title: Chart Type Matches The Data
gates.rule: Trend to line, comparison to bar, proportion to pie or donut - and no pie past five categories.

gates.title: Chart Colours Are Colourblind-Safe
gates.rule: No red/green-only pairing, and colour is supplemented by pattern, texture, or shape.

gates.title: A Table Alternative Exists
gates.rule: The data is available as a table or text summary, since a chart alone is unreadable to a screen reader.

gates.title: Legend Is Visible And Near The Chart
gates.rule: Not detached below a scroll fold. Where series can be toggled, the legend does it.

gates.title: Values Are Reachable Without Hover
gates.rule: Tooltips work on tap, and their content is keyboard-reachable. Small datasets label directly.

gates.title: Axes Are Labelled And Readable
gates.rule: Units named, ticks not cramped, labels not rotated into illegibility on mobile, time granularity stated.

gates.title: Charts Reflow On Small Screens
gates.rule: Horizontal bars instead of vertical, fewer ticks, simplified series - not a squeezed desktop chart.

gates.title: Empty, Loading, And Failed Chart States
gates.rule: No-data says so with guidance, loading shows a shaped skeleton rather than a bare axis frame, and a failure offers retry.

gates.title: Chart Contrast Meets Threshold
gates.rule: Data marks clear 3:1 against the background; data labels clear 4.5:1. Gridlines stay low-contrast so they do not compete.

gates.title: Chart Interactivity Is Keyboard-Reachable
gates.rule: Points, bars, and slices are focusable, with a text summary naming the chart's key insight.

gates.title: Large Datasets Aggregate
gates.rule: Past a thousand points, aggregate or sample and offer drill-down rather than rendering everything.

gates.title: Numbers Are Locale-Formatted
gates.rule: Numbers, dates, and currencies formatted for the locale on axes and labels.

gates.title: Data Over Decoration
gates.rule: No heavy gradients or shadows on data marks. Density is capped; split rather than cram.

gates.title: Chart Touch Targets Clear 44pt
gates.rule: Interactive points and segments have a 44pt tap area or expand on touch.

gates.title: Sortable Tables Announce Their Sort
gates.rule: aria-sort reflects the current column and direction.

gates.title: Tables Have A Small-Screen Answer
gates.rule: A table on a phone stacks, scrolls inside its own container, or drops to the columns that matter - it does not overflow the page.

gates.title: Action Feedback Is A Transient Toast, Bottom Right
gates.rule: The outcome of an action the visitor just took - a sign-in refused, an account made, something added to a cart, a record saved - is reported by a transient toast in the bottom-right corner, raised through one shared host and gone on its own. Not an inline banner pushed into the page: a coloured strip above a form moves every field below it the instant it appears, stays until some other code clears it, and reads as part of the page rather than as an answer to the click. Not a per-page one-off either, because that is how one product ends up with a green bar at the top of one route, a red panel inline on another, and no two of them behaving alike. One host, one corner, one lifetime.
gates.fix: Put one toast host in the shell and raise everything through it. Anchor it bottom right, give each toast a lifetime that clears it without being touched, and use the assertive live region for failures and the polite one for successes. Delete the inline banners and the per-page fixed one-offs as you go; leaving one behind is what the gate counts.
